note: Bins were fixed in DEFECT_TAXONOMY_PREREGISTRATION.md before any row was written. UNCLASSIFIED is not a dumping ground; it is the pre-registered test of whether the bin set carves anything. THRESHOLD DEFECT, found by the gate firing at n=30: the pre-registered W_C condition is an ABSOLUTE count (a bin >= 8), not a proportion. At n=22 that was 36% of the ledger; at n=30 a bin of 9 is 30% and the same threshold fires. An absolute threshold on a growing ledger makes ONE-JOINT-DOMINATES inevitable. It is NOT changed here -- choosing a threshold after seeing which verdict it produces is the one move this file exists to refuse. The verdict is reported as pre-registered, with the defect stated beside it.

defects.defect: the front page inferred '9 of 168 heads clear the exhaustive floor, SO single-head ablation resolves effects here perfectly well' -- written one step earlier
defects.operation: THE COUNT ESTABLISHES NOTHING. Beyond 2*sd a normal over 168 numbers gives 7.6 and a Laplace gives 9.9; observed 9. Excess kurtosis is +7.43, so 2*sd is a normal-theory cut on a distribution nothing like normal, and the tail is what such a distribution hands you for free. Leave-one-out (each head judged by a null excluding it) leaves the count at 9, so the circularity check ran and came back clean -- it is the INTERPRETATION that breaks. Every statement about ORDER survives, because a ranking needs no threshold. Predicted as ADVERSARY.md row A4 at MEDIUM severity; actual severity invalidated a front-page inference, so the calibration was under-severe

defects.defect: the surviving rank claim -- 'the published heads rank 10..143 of 168' -- was computed on RAW |drop|, while R9 had already established the floor GROWS with depth, and the published heads sit at mean layer 18.1 against the top nine's 21.0
defects.operation: CONTROLLED, and the control CONFIRMED rather than killed. Ranking each head against its own layer's sd leaves the normalised top nine DEEPER still (21.8), moves the published heads by at most 21 places of 168, and puts 0 of them in the top nine either way. The stronger form is an INVARIANCE: the two top-nines share only 6 of 9 members, so WHICH heads are top is normalisation-dependent, while the published heads' absence from both is not

defects.defect: the withdrawn quiet-layer item-noise bound reported '3 of 8 measurable'

The bound did not merely rest on a bad assumption -- it also got the number wrong, in the direction that made the instrument look weaker than it is. UNVERIFIED becomes CONFIRMED by a fit instrument, not by promotion of the earlier silence

defects.defect: headline.py's load() globbed every JSON in a results directory and assumed a measurement schema, so the FIRST REFUSAL ARTIFACT crashed the whole gate with a KeyError on 'layers'

defects.defect: the eight drop values the entire project is about had never been checked against a second implementation
defects.operation: REPRODUCE to 3.6e-06 under R10's exhaustive scan -- same items, same vocabulary, separately written runner. Float32 nondeterminism. Closure that could have failed and had never been run. The same comparison carries the method point: E132b asked about 8 heads and R10 about 336 on the same code path, 42x the questions for one 16-minute job, and asking about all of them is what produced every finding of the last five steps

defects.defect: the project's central claim is a MEASURED ZERO -- 0 of 8 distinguishable -- and no positive control for it had ever been stated, in violation of the repository's own rule that a measured zero is inadmissible until the same instrument has returned non-zero
defects.operation: IT PASSES, and the control was in the same run all along: 9 heads are BOTH resolvable at 2 sigma AND beyond the exhaustive floor, at 1.18x-2.54x the floor and 2.5x-22.1x their own SEM. Also a dynamic-range check that had never been run: for 167 of 168 heads the floor exceeds that head's own measurement noise. The exception is NAMED, not averaged away -- L26H7 has 2*SEM 0.4991 against a floor of 0.4870, so no verdict about it is possible at all

defects.defect: the distinguishability verdict uses the STUDIED BAND's own heads as the null -- a distribution of heads that DO things -- and the alternative null R1 originally used (the sham band, L0-7) had never been applied to the eight
defects.operation: PRE-REGISTERED >=4 of 8 clearing the sham floor as 'the reference class decides the verdict'; observed 3, DID NOT FIRE, so that claim is not made. But the shape is sharper: the two floors are 6.15x apart from reference class alone, and 78 of 168 band heads (46%) also clear the sham floor. Clearing it is not distinction, it is being in the second half of the network. With R9's depth result the reading is exact -- L22H7 is distinguishable from an early-layer head and indistinguishable from a late-layer one, so its ablation number carries DEPTH information, not ROLE information

defects.defect: 'clearing the sham floor is being in the second half of the network' -- written one step earlier as the interpretation of the 46% figure
defects.operation: TOO COARSE, and the direct measurement shows why. The per-layer clearing rate rises with depth (Spearman +0.645 over 28 layers) but NOT monotonically: it peaks at 83% in L16-L17 and falls back to 8% by L25, so L25 clears LESS often than L11. A hump, not a half. Two facts place the copy head exactly: L22's own rate is 42%, the band average, and within its layer L22H7 is the 5th of 5 heads that clear -- the smallest. And 4 of the 8 published heads live in the PEAK layers where 83% of heads clear, which is why they clear the sham floor and why it establishes nothing

defects.defect: the page promised a stranger can check every claim with no dependencies, and that path had not been re-tested since the gate grew from 11 files to 28 and gained a refusal artifact, two round directories and the provenance validator

It PASSES. The run also surfaced a state the page did not mention -- provenance reports 0 CONFIRMED because _PRODUCER changed in all 12 runners the same day -- now explained on the page rather than left to surprise the reader

defects.defect: the distinguishability statistic has always been |drop| > 2*sd, which silently places the null at ZERO. The studied band's null has mean +0.0479 = 0.20 sd: ablating a random late-layer head improves the correct-answer margin more often than it hurts, 100 positive vs 68 negative of 168
defects.operation: CORRECTED to |drop - mean| > 2*sd, and IT CHANGES THE HEADLINE COUNT: L16H3 goes 0.96x -> 1.06x and CLEARS, so the figure is 1 of 8, not 0 of 8. The proven copy head moves the other way, 0.27x -> 0.37x, and stays far inside. Across 168 band heads the count goes 9 -> 10. The offset was first shown NOT to be an intervention artifact: the sham band is centred (+0.0040, 0.10 sd, 51/45 signs) while the studied band is at 0.20 sd, so it grows with depth alongside the spread and is a fact about the late band rather than about zero-ablation

defects.defect: correcting the k=1 null's centring left every OTHER comparison uncentred, and one of them was the front page's OPENING LINE: '0 of those 9 are among the eight published heads'
defects.operation: THE CORRECTION OBLIGED A RE-RUN AND I HAD NOT DONE IT. Centred everywhere: the k=1 clearing set goes 9 -> 10 and the tenth is L16H3, A PUBLISHED HEAD, so the opening line's '0 of those 9' becomes '1 of those 10'. The k=5 circuit goes 1.45x -> 1.65x, and the centred ratio turns out to be exactly |z|/2 -- so 'x floor' and 'z' were two names for one quantity with one mis-centred, printed side by side. The sham-band comparison is UNCHANGED at 3 of 8 because that null's mean is +0.0040, which is the evidence the rule was applied everywhere rather than where it flattered. Uncentred forms are still emitted so each correction can be read against what it corrects

defects.defect: the task was described as a BINDING task for twelve rounds. Every runner picks the query as the first single-token person and every binding assigns all eight, so the query is always Alice; fact lines follow a fixed order, so Alice's fact is always line 0
defects.operation: THE CORRECT ANSWER IS ALWAYS THE ROOM IN THE FIRST SENTENCE. 'Copy the room from line 0' scores 100% without matching a name. The labels are balanced -- the four rooms take 23.5%-26.2% over 400 seeds -- so it is the STRUCTURE that is degenerate, not the answer key. It does not break any comparison BETWEEN heads, since all face the same task; it breaks the DESCRIPTION. L22H7 may be copying from position 0 rather than resolving a name, and no measurement here can distinguish those, because the two strategies agree on every item the task contains

defects.defect: the task audit's own import guard was `except Exception: return None`, and it swallowed a NameError (headline.py had no `import sys`) so the entire section vanished from the output with no error
defects.operation: A GUARD THAT TURNS A BUG INTO AN ABSENCE -- the exact pattern this repository keeps finding in other people's checks, hiding one of its own for a run. Narrowed to ImportError and made loud: it now refuses with a message rather than returning None, because reporting nothing looks identical to reporting no problem

defects.defect: the fixed-position degeneracy depends on the TOKENIZER -- the query is the first single-token person -- so different models could have been asked about different people at different line indices, making R1's cross-model ratio a comparison of two different tasks
defects.operation: PROBED and UNIFORM. Across 8 model x vocabulary cells the distinct query line indices are [0]: single-token counts differ (8, 8, 6, 4 of 8) but Alice is single-token under every tokenizer tested, so every model is asked about line 0. Cross-model comparisons stay commensurable. The degeneracy is not model-specific -- it is everywhere

defects.defect: the first version of this probe REIMPLEMENTED the runner's tokenization instead of reusing it, omitting the prefix_len adjustment, and reported 0 of 8 single-token persons for phi-3.5-mini
defects.operation: WRONG, and caught only because the actual run had already PRINTED 6/8 to its job log. The disagreement with a number the object had emitted is the entire reason it surfaced. Same 'match rule is not the concept' defect this repository keeps finding in other people's checks, committed while investigating that exact class. defects.operation: THE VERDICT SPACE COLLAPSED TO ONE REACHABLE OUTCOME AT n=26, forty-four rows ago. defects.defect: R2's clears_2sd verdicts used |d_top| > 2*sd with the null placed at zero -- the same defect corrected in R1 -- and R2 had never been audited the way R1 has
defects.operation: CENTRED, and the verdicts SURVIVE: 4 of 5 either way. Every one of the five nulls is off-centre and all NEGATIVE, from -0.19 to -0.62 sd, further than R1's band at +0.20 and in the opposite sense -- ablating random heads HURTS induction while it HELPED the room-task margin. d_top is negative too, so centring makes clearing harder, and the count holds because the effects are 6.5x to 18.7x the floor. This also yields the sharpest available statement of why R1 and R2 disagreed: on one scale, R1's eight run 1.06 down to 0.01 and R2's valid four run 1.20 up to 18.68 -- the distributions barely touch, and the disagreement is about EFFECT SIZE, not method

defects.defect: R2's task has the same fixed-offset degeneracy R13 found in R1's, and it had never been audited. Sequences are core+core with T=64 CONSTANT, so the answer at position T+i always sits exactly T positions back -- a head attending at a constant distance solves it with no content matching
defects.operation: THE TASK CANNOT DISTINGUISH positional copying from prefix-matching, because the two agree on every sequence it contains. Ids are uniform random over 39000 so there is no LEXICAL shortcut, but the POSITIONAL one is complete. Does not break any comparison between the top-k and random-k heads -- they face the same task, so the floor, the 4-of-5 count and the effect sizes stand. Breaks calling them prefix-matching or induction heads as a claim about CONTENT. Repair is R14's shape: vary T per sequence

defects.defect: the head-SELECTION criterion is defined by the degenerate feature: induction_scores measures attention from position i to position i-T+1, a fixed offset, and its own docstring calls that a 'prefix-matching score'
defects.operation: THE NAME ASSERTS CONTENT MATCHING; THE COMPUTATION MEASURES DISTANCE. A label carried where a derivation was needed, inside the function that chooses which heads the entire round is about -- so selection and readout are degenerate in the same direction, and a constant-distance head would score maximally on both

defects.defect: the front page opened with FIVE correction blocks before stating what the project found, and the first runnable command sat 5685 words in, at line 513 of 994
defects.operation: MEASURED, not suspected. A reader forming a mental model in the 1-3 minutes the review standard calls L2 received, in order: the task is not what we said, R14 resolved something, every number is in one configuration, R12 settled the hump -- and only then the finding. The page read as a chronology of the author's corrections rather than as an inferential path, and an L2 failure caps the artifact because nobody reaches the depth where the rigour is. FIXED BY INSERTION, NOT REORDERING: the finding, the runnable command and a pointer to the six-version retraction ladder now sit above everything, and nothing was deleted or moved. The finding carries its own retraction pointer inline, so a reader who stops there still knows it was corrected six times

defects.defect: 'ablation magnitude and mechanistic role are close to unrelated on this task' -- a claim about a RELATIONSHIP between two variables, promoted to the top of the front page one step earlier, resting on exactly ONE head with an independently established role
defects.operation: n=1 ON THE ROLE AXIS. L22H7 is the only established mechanism here; five of the other seven were read-head CANDIDATES, and a candidate is a hypothesis, so finding hypotheses fail to clear a floor is close to tautological (already conceded as ADVERSARY.md row A1). One point is an anecdote, not a relationship. THE REVERSE DIRECTION IS SUPPORTED AND IS NOW WHAT THE PAGE SAYS: of the 10 heads that clear the exhaustive floor, the first published one is the 10th, and 7 of the 10 clear by HELPING the model -- that rests on 10 points and needs no second known mechanism. The asymmetry is the honest finding and is stronger than the symmetric claim it replaces

defects.defect: the prior-effects file's note -- written by me -- said the eight were 'five read-head CANDIDATES, one independently proven copy head' and two unlabelled. I had never opened the source experiment to check
defects.operation: WRONG COMPOSITION. E132b's `sel` dict has SEVEN keys and its `drop` dict has eight: seven selected read-head candidates plus L22H7, which E132 ranked FIRST on room attention and which was added externally. Self-report about a source experiment, believed for fifteen rounds because the file it lived in was mine

defects.defect: fifteen rounds treated 'the eight published effects' as a given set without asking how it was chosen -- the set is the heads ATTENTION picked, and the audit measures them with ABLATION, a two-instrument comparison that had never been run
defects.operation: THE INSTRUMENTS ANTI-CORRELATE. Over 168 band heads: Spearman(|centred ablation|, room attention) = -0.1885 and (name attention) = -0.3952. L15H7 is 168th of 168 on BOTH attention criteria and 9th by ablation. Top-5 by name attention land at ablation ranks 129, 137, 157, 88, 167. NOT A DISCOVERY -- attention as an unreliable proxy for causal importance is established background, stated as such in arXiv 2504.13752's abstract, and the literature query's positive control is reported (one relevant hit, noisy, no completeness claimed). What R16 adds is the consequence for this audit: the eight were selected by exactly the proxy known to fail, which gives 'the loudest heads were never identified' a named cause

defects.defect: R16 correlated attention with |centred ablation| only. The absolute value discards the sign, which this project had already shown matters -- 100 positive against 68 negative in the band, 7 of 9 clearing heads clearing by HELPING -- and a reader given only a negative number would fill in 'high-attention heads help when ablated'
defects.operation: IT IS A MAGNITUDE EFFECT, NOT A DIRECTION ONE. Signed Spearman is about three times weaker: room -0.0583 against -0.1885, name -0.1142 against -0.3952. Attention picks heads that do LESS, in either direction. The top name-attention quartile does carry a direction -- 9 positive against 33 negative, mean signed drop -0.0311 -- so those heads do tend to hurt when ablated, which is what a real role predicts; their effects are simply small, which is why they rank low on |ablation|. Both forms now emitted so the negative number cannot be misread

defects.defect: R12's verdict is a claim about DEPTH, measured with an instrument whose sensitivity is monotone in depth and was never controlled. Ablation zeroes the FINAL POSITION ONLY, so a head's writes at positions 0..n-2 survive; the layers that can read them number NL-1-L, which is NL-1 at layer 0 and ZERO at the last layer where the measurement is complete. (NL-1-L)/NL is a FRACTION OF DEPTH -- the exact shape of RELATIVE, R12's surviving hypothesis -- so the confound manufactures RELATIVE out of ABSOLUTE, and the two predictions were 5.6 layers apart with the later one winning
defects.operation: POSITIVE CONTROL RUN, AND IT FIRES AGAINST THE CONFOUND WITHOUT CLEARING IT. A bias-only profile -- flat truth times monotone sensitivity -- must be MAXIMAL at the last layer. qwen2.5-3b clears at 0.000 there, its global minimum, against a peak of 0.562 at L26; qwen2.5-1.5b is 0.167 against 0.833 at L16. So the bias does not run the SHAPE. It still moves the CENTROID, which is a first moment of truth times sensitivity and is pulled late whatever the truth looks like, and the control cannot separate 'sensitivity is flat' from 'the last layers do nothing'. R12's RELATIVE is therefore UNVERIFIED -- not OVERTURNED, because the shape control is real evidence, and not CONFIRMED, because the confound points exactly the way the winner points. The settling run is pre-registered on R12's page: ablate at ALL positions and see whether the centroid moves earlier by a fixed FRACTION or a fixed NUMBER of layers. Separately, 'final position only' is now stated in the front page's scope line, where it was missing: the unit measured throughout this repository is not a head but a head's write at the final position. Filed under INTERVENTION and not a new bin: the gate refused 'CONFOUND' as unregistered, which is the taxonomy doing its job -- inventing a category name mid-flight is the drift the schema exists to prevent. The defect is a property of the INTERVENTION itself, which cuts at one position

defects.defect: the exhaustive floor 0.4870 was quoted throughout this repository as a property of the model and the band. R15's pre-registered third reading -- per-answer-line floors -- shows it is a function of the task's headroom: per-line floors span 1.66x (0.3011 to 0.4997) and track the per-line baseline margin at Spearman +0.8810 over 8 lines. It was measured at baseline margin 4.477
defects.operation: SUBLINEARLY, WHICH CUTS BOTH WAYS AND BOTH ARE NOW STATED. Across lines the margin spans 7.54x while the floor spans only 1.66x, so the ABSOLUTE floor is comparatively robust -- which is what a noise floor should be if it measures head-to-head variability rather than task headroom. But floor/margin spans 5.84x (0.108 to 0.633), so `x floor` -- the unit this repository ranks its eight published heads in -- IS NOT PORTABLE ACROSS TASK CONFIGURATIONS. Separately, the pre-registered PRIMARY landed in the middle band: Spearman on |centred drop| +0.6092 against thresholds of 0.7 and 0.3 committed before the run, with the signed version at +0.7175 straddling it; both are reported and neither is claimed, because picking the statistic that clears is a narrative. The population confound was checked and cleared by measurement, not argument: R15 changed line order AND the correctness filter, but R14's A_orig=1.000 makes the filter a measured no-op on the comparison arm, and the two files share draw_seed 20260727, 120 items, 4 rooms and sham band [0,7]

THE VALUE WAS NOT IN THE FORECAST: A4 was resolved by the file itself and scored the author under-severe, and A7's act of being written found the real problem. defects.operation: IT MOVES THE HEADLINE. Uncentred: Spearman +0.9778, RMS displacement 10.22, largest mover L23H3 at 43 places, L22H7 56->96. CENTRED, which is what the front page reports: Spearman +0.9570, RMS 14.23, and L22H7 moves 41->160 -- 119 places, THE LARGEST MOVE OF ALL 168 HEADS. defects.defect: the depth-bias argument was labelled D8 -- 'logical from checked premises' -- and asserted that the instrument's sensitivity is MONOTONE in depth and therefore that the confound MANUFACTURES RELATIVE out of ABSOLUTE. Only two things are structural: at the last layer the missed cross-token paths are zero, and at earlier layers such paths MAY exist with NL-1-L possible readers. A COUNT OF POSSIBLE READERS IS NOT A MAGNITUDE OF MISSED INFLUENCE
defects.operation: RETRACTED TO D5. The sign, magnitude and monotonicity of the missed term were never established, and cancellation, backup heads, negative heads and interaction terms each break the inference -- single-component effects are known to be badly non-additive, with some context-dependent heads having near-zero singleton effect and acting only alongside others. The claim the page is entitled to is that RELATIVE is COMPATIBLE WITH an uncontrolled intervention-support confound that may covary with normalized depth. That keeps the verdict at UNVERIFIED, which it already was, and withdraws the mechanism claim dressed as a derivation. No number on the page changes; what the numbers are allowed to mean does. Raised by Ivan, who is not sampled from the weights that wrote it -- the first external correction this project has had

defects.defect: R18's page and the reported headline called L17H0 at rank 4 of 168 under I_all 'the result'. It is the maximum of EIGHT pre-specified heads surfaced by scanning 168, tested without any correction. Its one-head exact randomization p is 0.0296, which is 0.2367 after Bonferroni over the eight tested -- a POST-SELECTION DESCRIPTIVE TAIL, not a finding. Ivan named this exact failure mode before the run: scanning many components requires multiple-comparison correction or an explicit post-selection label
defects.operation: AND THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT HAD NEVER BEEN RUN IN THIS PROJECT. Every earlier round compared heads one at a time against a SCALAR floor whose reference class does not hold LAYER fixed. The right question is whether the PRE-SPECIFIED SET of eight is more extreme than a random set from the SAME LAYERS. T_pub = mean |tau - mu_band| over the set; the null replaces each published head with a uniform random head from its own layer, 50,000 times. I_final: T_pub 0.1154 against a null median of 0.1670, p = 0.7994. I_all: 0.3196 against 0.4004, p = 0.6782. NOT ENRICHED UNDER EITHER, AND BELOW THE NULL MEDIAN IN BOTH -- the eight are on average LESS extreme than same-layer random heads. Instrument checked before the null was believed: positive control on the actual top-8 gives p = 0.00004, and 200 random matched sets fall under 0.05 at a rate of 0.035 against a nominal 0.05. Layer matching is load-bearing: the eight sit in L16-L22 and magnitude varies strongly with depth, so an unmatched null manufactures enrichment from position alone. Both arms are heavy-tailed, excess kurtosis 7.31 and 6.67, which is why the percentile replaces 2*sd

defects.defect: the repository quotes '100 positive, 68 negative of 168' to characterise the band's sign distribution, and that split is RAW. Every verdict here uses the CENTRED statistic, and centred on the band mean +0.0479 the split is 64 above and 104 below. The qualitative reading INVERTS: raw says 'ablation hurts more often than it helps', centred says 'most heads are LESS harmful than the average head'
defects.operation: BOTH ARE TRUE OF DIFFERENT QUANTITIES AND ONLY ONE MATCHES THE ANALYSIS. Annotated in place at both sites rather than replaced, because the raw split is what the sign-matters argument was originally built on and deleting it would hide that the argument was made on a different quantity from the one the tests use. The centred counts are now emitted so either can be checked

defects.defect: the eight heads were SELECTED, causally EVALUATED and then AUDITED on the same 120 items, and nothing in this repository said so. From source: e132_read_head.py:29 uses SEEDS = range(3000,3300) for selection, e132b_read_head_causal.py:27 uses the same range for the causal evaluation, and R10_exhaustive/run.py:72 uses range(3000,3400) taking the first 120 that pass the same baseline-correct filter -- which R14 measured as rejecting nothing on this task for this model. R11's set B, range(3400,3800), is the ONLY independent item set in the entire project
defects.operation: IT CUTS BOTH WAYS AND BOTH ARE NOW STATED. The 'not enriched' null is STRENGTHENED: the eight fail to beat matched-layer random sets on the very data they were chosen on, with full home advantage. But every head-level number here except set B is computed on the selection data, which is a scope on all of it. THE SHRINKAGE TEST ON THE INDEPENDENT ITEMS: sum-ratio 0.8425 against a matched-layer null median of 1.0180, p 0.0150; mean-of-ratios 0.8257 against 1.0085, p 0.0098; MEDIAN-of-ratios 0.9919 against 1.0135, p 0.2769. Two of three fire and the median does not, so all three are reported rather than one being chosen -- L16H3 and L22H7 carry 75% of sum|c_A|, which makes the sum-ratio essentially a two-head statistic. THE SET-LEVEL WINNER'S CURSE IS NOT A SET PROPERTY: L22H7 alone retains 0.0401 of its centred effect on independent items, the lowest of all 168 band heads at the 0.0th percentile, exact one-head p 0.0118, against a band median retention of 1.02 and its own eleven layer-mates at 0.59 to 1.22. That is what the rank move 41 -> 160 was. RTM control: the eight are BELOW the matched-layer null median on set A, so regression to the mean predicts they shrink LESS than random and the observed direction runs against that prediction rather than being explained by it

defects.defect: R19's pre-registration -- the first confirmatory design in this repository, written two hours earlier -- carried THREE thresholds that were words rather than numbers. H-position asked for 'median head-wise ICC across positions HIGH' with no value, and for the published heads' position interaction to be 'NOT LARGER than matched controls' with no statistic and no cutoff. H-published asked for 'confirmatory effect direction MATCHING THE ORIGINAL CLAIM' while the eight heads' claimed directions were never enumerated anywhere. A pre-registration with a vague threshold is not pre-registered on that axis: it is a place where a verdict can be inserted after the fact, which is the one thing the file exists to prevent
defects.operation: AMENDED BEFORE THE RUN, WHICH IS THE ONLY TIME AN AMENDMENT IS LEGITIMATE -- R19 was still queued behind pueue 232 and results/ was empty. (1) ICC: median over heads of ICC(1,1) across the 8 positions >= 0.50, variance components over the 64 base instances, and the 0.50 is declared CHOSEN rather than derived. (2) Position interaction: P_h = RMS over positions of pi_h,p, set statistic = mean over the eight, null = replace each published head with a uniform random head FROM ITS OWN LAYER, 50,000 replicates; pass requires one-sided p >= 0.05, and p < 0.05 in the other tail is reported as 'the eight are MORE position-dependent', a finding rather than a failure. (3) Direction enumerated: all eight entered as read-head candidates plus one externally-known copy head, so the claimed direction for every one is HURT -- tau_h > 0 under drop = margin_base - margin_ablated -- one-sided throughout, no per-head exceptions. FOURTH, ADDED BECAUSE D91 MADE IT NECESSARY: a discovery/confirmation split of the 64 base instances, 0..31 nominate and 32..63 judge, deterministic from BUILD_SEED and needing no extra run. The eight are exempt and judged on all 64 because a prior experiment on a disjoint item family specified them; any head R19 itself surfaces is nominated on the first half and tested on the second, or reported as post-selection descriptive

defects.defect: Amendment 1 to R19's pre-registration, committed roughly twenty minutes earlier, enumerated the claimed direction for all eight heads as HURT and made the test one-sided. THREE OF THE EIGHT HAVE NEGATIVE DROPS IN THE SOURCE -- L16H3 at -0.4668 which is the largest effect of the set, L22H7 at -0.1317 which is the copy head, and L17H7 at -0.0352 -- so under drop = margin_base - margin_ablated those three HELP. A one-sided HURT test would have been aimed at the wrong tail for exactly them and would have systematically failed to detect them, which is a false null in this repository's own favour
defects.operation: REPLACED WITH TWO-SIDED FOR ALL EIGHT, before the run, with results/ still empty and R19 queued behind pueue 232. The reason is not convenience: E132b made NO PER-HEAD DIRECTIONAL CLAIM to enumerate, and taking the source's OBSERVED signs as the 'claimed direction' is circular because it is the same data the test would then run on. All eight reproduce in R10 to < 1e-4 on the same base margin 4.4768, so the sign convention is confirmed rather than assumed. Amendment 1's own last sentence said 'if a head's original claim was directionally different, this document is wrong and that is recorded rather than adjusted' -- that escape hatch is the one being used

defects.defect: E132b's own verdict field reads W-READ-REDUNDANT. The source experiment concluded that the read heads are REDUNDANT -- that individually they do not carry the effect -- and its own largest reported drop is L16H3 at 10.4% of the base margin. This repository has framed itself as pointing a measurement at PUBLISHED POSITIVE CLAIMS and finding them inside the noise. For seven of the eight there was no positive claim to deflate
defects.operation: THE AUDIT'S NULL IS CONSISTENT WITH THE SOURCE'S OWN CONCLUSION rather than a correction of it, and the framing is now stated that way. THE CORRECTION MUST NOT OVERSHOOT IN THE OTHER DIRECTION AND THAT IS STATED TOO: E132b never measured a reference distribution at all, never ran a matched-layer set randomization, never tested the all-position intervention, and never used a disjoint item set -- those four results are this repository's and are unaffected. defects.defect: the repository measured four separate floors -- across items, across intervention support, across task position, across layer band -- and never once asked the question that makes them a claim rather than a list: DOES A SCALAR FLOOR TRANSPORT? Every verdict here applies a floor measured in one configuration as though the decision rule it defines means the same thing in another
defects.operation: MEASURED, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT IS ALSO THE DISCRIMINATOR. Transport A's whole rule |x - mu_A| > floor_A into three configurations each differing in exactly one factor. Item sample only: 10/168 both ways, ratio 1.00 -- so the instrument IS stable across draws and a failure elsewhere is not sampling noise. Intervention support only: own reference says 14/168, the transported rule says 33/168, ratio 2.36. Task/answer position only: own says 12/168, transported says 6/168, ratio 0.50. THE TWO FAILURES POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, so a scalar floor is not merely imprecise -- its bias depends on which way the configuration moved and no safety factor fixes it. This is the one result in the repository that is about the METHOD rather than about the eight heads, and it is what survives D94's finding that seven of the eight carried no positive claim to deflate. HONEST LIMIT: the `own` column is the same 2-sigma rule on a heavy-tailed distribution, so this compares two applications of one rule rather than calibrating against a nominal alpha; one model, one band, one task family, k=1, one contrast per axis

defects.defect: the transport result committed one step earlier moved mu_A and floor_A together, so its 2.36x and 0.50x conflated two different failures with two different remedies: the CENTRE of the reference distribution not travelling, which a local re-centring fixes cheaply, and the SCALE not travelling, which means the floor is not a number that can be carried at all
defects.operation: DECOMPOSED, AND IT SHARPENS THE CLAIM RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. Transporting the SCALE only, with a local re-centring, leaves the miscalibration almost untouched: I_all 32 against its own 14, shuffled 5 against its own 12. Transporting the CENTRE only, with the local scale, is nearly calibrated: 12 against 14 and 13 against 12. SO RE-CENTRING FIXES NOTHING AND THE LOCAL SCALE FIXES ALMOST EVERYTHING. The confound written before the test -- that mu and floor are not independent, so a centre-driven verdict could be spread wearing a location mask -- is refuted in the useful direction: the centre moves by almost exactly the same factor as the scale (1.98x against 2.01x for I_all) AND IT DOES NOT MATTER, because the centre is about 10% of the half-width (0.0946 against 0.9766) and shifting it barely moves a threshold sitting at +-floor. THE SCALE IS THE ESTIMAND, which is a sharper statement than 'a scalar floor does not transport'. World B -- centre-driven, cheap fix -- is killed

defects.defect: the transport table had three axes -- item sample, intervention support, task position -- and omitted the LAYER BAND, which carries the largest variation in the repository (6.15x) and is the only axis where the REVERSE direction is testable because both regions come from one result file. Separately, the conclusion 'the centre is about 10% of the half-width so it does not matter' was measured ON THE BAND and stated without that scope
defects.operation: THE LAYER AXIS FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Sham L0-7 judged by the band's rule detects 0 against its own 4, ratio 0.00 -- you see nothing. Band L14-27 judged by the sham rule calls 78 against its own 10, ratio 7.80 -- 46% of the band. AND IT CORRECTS THE PRECEDING SECTION: centre-only transport there gives 8 against its own 4, because the centre SHIFT is 55.5% of the destination's scale rather than a few percent. THE UNIFYING QUANTITY IS |mu_dest - mu_src| / floor_dest: 0.1% for new items with centre-only ratio 1.00, 2.2% for shuffled with 1.08, 4.8% for I_all with 0.86, and 55.5% for the layer axis with 2.00. The centre matters exactly when its shift is large relative to the destination's scale, so 'the scale is the estimand' is itself scoped -- true on three of these four axes and false on the fourth. n=4 contrasts, and what makes four points worth stating is a MECHANISM rather than a trend: a threshold at +-f is insensitive to a shift small relative to f and stops being insensitive when it is not

defects.defect: the transport result was framed as a discovery -- 'a scalar floor does not transport' -- when transporting an ABSOLUTE cutoff gives a count that depends only on the destination's distribution, so the statement is trivially true of ANY absolute cutoff whenever the destination differs. Verified rather than argued: A's 2sd cutoff 0.4870 and A's own 5.95th-percentile cutoff 0.5147 agree on A by construction and give near-identical counts everywhere else (10/33/6 against 8/32/5). THE FAILURE IS NOT ABOUT 2*sd, and the section was written more dramatically than the arithmetic supports
defects.operation: REFRAMED TO WHAT IS ACTUALLY NON-TRIVIAL: that it transports PERFECTLY across item samples (10 against 10, ratio 1.00), which is not automatic and is what makes the other rows interpretable; the MAGNITUDES AND DIRECTIONS, 2.36x inflate and 0.50x deflate and 7.80x/0.00 on the layer axis; and the scale/centre decomposition with the |delta mu| / floor_dest predictor. AND THE META-SEPARATOR IS NOW STATED ONCE, WHICH IT NEVER HAD BEEN: 'does the floor transport' presupposes a right answer to 'how many heads are real', and there is no ground truth here. Transport a PROCEDURE instead of a NUMBER -- take the top 5.95% of the local band -- and it returns 5.95% everywhere by construction: it cannot fail and it cannot be validated. Calibration in this repository means SELF-CONSISTENCY, not correctness, and nothing on disk separates 'the floor is conditional' from 'we have no way to know what the floor should be'. What would separate them: a synthetic model with a constructed ground-truth circuit, or heads whose role is established by path patching, transduction or causal scrubbing rather than by the same magnitude statistic being audited. That experiment is not in this repository and is not scheduled

defects.defect: the repository calls itself an AUDIT. An audit presupposes the auditor is more reliable than the audited, and nothing here establishes that -- R16 says explicitly that two instruments disagreeing does not rank them. After D100 established every role claim traces to ATTENTION, the framing asserts a hierarchy the repository's own results refuse
defects.operation: THE ARBITER QUESTION ANSWERED FROM NUMBERS ALREADY ON DISK. Ablation is interventional where attention is observational, which would privilege it. BUT R6 MEASURED THIS INTERVENTION AS SUBSTANTIALLY OFF-MANIFOLD: readability = |positive control| / band sd gives zero 2.35 against mean 1.03 and resample 0.77 on qwen2.5-1.5b, and zero 10.07 against 2.38 and 1.57 on qwen2.5-3b, with median ratios 0.24x and 0.22x over 3 informative cells. Replacing a head's output with its own mean or a resampled value recovers only 22-24% of what zeroing does, so roughly three quarters of the zeroing effect is the absence of any plausible activation rather than the head's contribution. R8 adds that randdir's positive control SIGN-INVERTS on 4 of 4 models and its order gate was NOT MET at 1 of 4. An intervention into a state the model never occupies does not establish counterfactual dependence on the state it does. NEITHER INSTRUMENT ARBITRATES: this is a two-instrument disagreement with both defects measured, which is a smaller claim than 'an audit' and the one the evidence carries. n is small, three informative cells across four models, and the page says so

defects.defect: D101 established that zeroing is roughly 4x off-manifold, which threatens the transport headline: if the floor's conditionality is a property of ZEROING rather than of ABLATION, the claim is about one intervention and not about ablation baselines. defects.operation: WORLD B IS DEAD AND THE DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE WORRY. Band/sham floor ratios by arm: internlm2-1.8b 0.98 zero against 2.81 mean and 2.64 resample; phi-3.5-mini 12.27 against 2132.73 and 2046.29; qwen2.5-1.5b 4.31 against 815.46 and 1144.26; qwen2.5-3b 6.73 against 125.10 and 113.21. ON 4 OF 4 MODELS THE ON-MANIFOLD ARMS ARE MORE LAYER-DEPENDENT THAN ZEROING. The conditional-reference-distribution claim survives the off-manifold objection. BUT THE MECHANISM IS UNVERIFIED AND THE PAGE SAYS SO: the on-manifold sham floors collapse to 1e-5 to 4e-6, which R6 already flagged as DEGENERATE, so 'early-layer heads contribute nothing recoverable' and 'these arms lack the dynamic range to resolve early layers' are the same observation with different attitude and nothing separates them. AND ONE MODEL DISSENTS ON THE ZERO ARM: internlm2-1.8b's ratio is 0.98, band and sham floors identical under zeroing, so 'the floor varies with layer' is 3 of 4 models rather than 4 of 4 -- and that is the model whose sham region was already flagged as non-inert. FINALLY, TWO ESTIMATORS OF THE SAME QUANTITY DISAGREE AND BOTH ARE REPORTED: R6's 4.31 for qwen2.5-1.5b is a k=1 estimate from 30 draws over 12 heads, while the 6.15 used earlier is exhaustive over every head in each region -- the R1 to R10 sampling story again, and neither is presented as the number

defects.defect: an outside critique said R6's displacement_ratio = ||x-xbar||/||x|| cannot answer whether mean-ablation is near-identity, because a small displacement can lie along a very high-gain direction of W_O and a large one can land in its approximate nullspace. The critique was accepted in prose and never measured, although both halves are computable from the weights alone -- no GPU, no activations
defects.operation: MEASURED, AND THE TWO HALVES SEPARATE. For a per-head displacement the functional version is r_out = ||W_h d|| / ||W_h x||, and since numerator and denominator pass through the same block, r_out/r is bounded in [1/kappa, kappa] with kappa the condition number of W_h = W_O[:, h*128:(h+1)*128]. Over the 168 band heads, each block 1536x128: condition number min 2.82, p25 4.31, MEDIAN 5.86, p75 7.61, max 17.67 at L27H10; stable rank (sum sigma)^2/(sum sigma^2) MEDIAN 117.2 OF 128 DIMENSIONS. SO THE NULLSPACE HALF IS REFUTED -- at stable rank 117/128 there is essentially no nullspace to land in -- AND THE HIGH-GAIN HALF IS BOUNDED at about 6x median rather than unbounded. displacement_ratio is indeed not a sufficient statistic for functional displacement, which is the critique's point and it stands; R6's verdict was already UNDECIDABLE and this does not change it, it explains part of why. THE BOUND IS LOOSE AND THE PAGE SAYS SO: [1/kappa, kappa] is a worst case over arbitrary directions, while the real displacement is item-to-item variation of a live activation and most likely lies in high-variance directions. Tightening needs the activations, which were never stored -- R6's diagnostic keeps mean_norm, sd_norm, cv and displacement_ratio only, over L14-27. THE SAME ABSENCE CLOSES D102's OPEN QUESTION: whether the on-manifold arms' sham collapse means 'no contribution' or 'no resolution' cannot be settled from disk either, because that diagnostic never covered L0-7, so the UNVERIFIED there is now CHECKED as unverifiable from current data rather than merely asserted

defects.defect: the repository mandated the empirical conditional randomization percentile in place of 2*sd, and never checked that the mandated method can answer its own surviving question. '10 of 168 clear the exhaustive floor' is the last positive count on the front page and it is a 2-sigma number on a distribution with excess kurtosis 7.31 -- exactly the case the page says 2-sigma does not test
defects.operation: RECOMPUTED LEAVE-ONE-OUT, AND THE RESOLUTION LIMIT IS THE FINDING. An empirical null built from the same 168 values has minimum attainable p = 1/169 = 0.0059, while Bonferroni at alpha 0.05 needs 0.00030 -- UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- and BH-FDR returns ZERO discoveries. Uncorrected empirical p <= 0.05 gives 8 of 168 against the published 10. AND THE P-VALUES THEMSELVES SHOW WHY: the eight smallest are 0.0060, 0.0119, 0.0179, 0.0238, 0.0298, 0.0357, 0.0417, 0.0476, which is 1/167, 2/167, 3/167 and so on. An empirical null built from the population being tested converts every p into a RANK DIVIDED BY n, so the test has no resolution beyond ordering. ZERO DISCOVERIES IS A RESOLUTION LIMIT, NOT AN ABSENCE, and the limit was computed before the test rather than read off it. THE SET-LEVEL TEST DOES HAVE RESOLUTION and the difference is instructive: its null is GENERATED by 50,000 matched-layer resamples rather than BEING the population, which is why it can return 0.0296 for a single head and 0.6817 for the set. Per-head significance needs a resampled null or a larger reference class; a count at a fixed threshold does not. PRECISE STATUS OF '10 of 168': a descriptive count at a chosen threshold, 8 under the repository's own uncorrected preferred method, 0 under any correction where 0 is an artifact of n. THIS DOES NOT TOUCH THE TRANSPORT RESULT, which compares counts under a FIXED rule across configurations and never claims per-head significance

defects.defect: the matched-layer set randomization -- the test that carries this repository's strongest statement, that the eight are NOT enriched -- draws replacement heads WITH REPLACEMENT while the observed set cannot repeat a head. The eight sit in layer multiset {16:1, 17:3, 18:1, 19:2, 22:1}, so three come from L17 and a with-replacement draw can pick the same L17 head twice against a published set of eight DISTINCT heads
defects.operation: THE DIRECTION WAS PREDICTED BEFORE MEASURING AND CONFIRMED. Sampling with replacement gives the set mean a larger variance, since there is no finite-population correction, so the null is WIDER than the correct one and the test is CONSERVATIVE for detecting enrichment. Measured over 50,000 replicates: null sd ratio 1.0313 on I_final and 1.0449 on I_all; drawing distinct-per-layer moves p from 0.7994 to 0.8069 and from 0.6817 to 0.6917 -- BOTH AWAY FROM SIGNIFICANCE. So the reported null result is safe and the correct version is further from significance than the published one. The magnitude is about 0.01 on p and changes no conclusion, which is why both are emitted rather than one being silently replaced. HAD THE RESULT BEEN POSITIVE the same defect would have been ANTI-conservative, which is the reason it is worth filing at all

defects.defect: the front page's clone-and-verify promise said the handle runs in 2.6 s on a stock python3. Re-measured: 41.26 s, peak 38 MB -- 16x slower than advertised. The 2.6 s was measured once on 2026-07-28 against a version that had none of the randomization tests added since, and the page kept quoting it while the handle grew
defects.operation: RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN RE-TUNED. The cost is four 50,000-replicate matched-layer nulls plus an 80,000-evaluation calibration loop, all added in the last several steps. Cutting replicates would have made the number true again by MOVING EVERY p-VALUE, which is churn dressed as a fix -- so the page now states 41.26 s and names the cause. THE TRADE IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: every randomization test that makes a claim checkable also makes the handle slower. THE CLASS OF FAILURE IS THE ONE THIS REPOSITORY DOCUMENTS ELSEWHERE: a number measured once and never re-measured while the thing it describes kept growing -- the same shape as the detector false-pass rate rising from 17.2% to 24.3% as the reference set grew, which was caught only because a prediction file happened to quote it

defects.defect: Amendment 1 to R19's pre-registration committed H-position to a median head-wise ICC(1,1) across the 8 positions. AN ICC NEEDS THE VARIANCE COMPONENTS, WHICH NEED THE BASE-BY-POSITION CELLS, and the runner recorded only the two marginal means -- per position over bases, and per base over positions. Marginal means cannot produce an ICC. So the pre-registration had committed a threshold against a statistic that would never be computable from its own output
defects.operation: CAUGHT BY WRITING THE ANALYSIS BEFORE THE DATA EXISTED, which is the entire reason to do that. results/ held only the n_base=2 smoke file and the 64-base run was still QUEUED, so the runner could be fixed without invalidating anything: it now accumulates a base x position tensor alongside the two margins, costing 336*2*64*8*3 floats or about 12 MB of JSON. The analysis reports NOT COMPUTABLE rather than substituting a different statistic when a result file lacks base_pos, so an older file cannot silently be scored by a proxy. AND THE BROADER POINT IS THE REASON THIS STEP HAPPENED AT ALL: pre-registered PROSE fixes thresholds, but pre-registered CODE fixes the estimators, the aggregation, the bootstrap unit and the tie-breaking -- every place a verdict can move after the fact without touching a single stated number. analyze.py is committed with results/ still empty, and its header says so

defects.defect: L22H7's copy-head label -- the only claimed role in this repository, and load-bearing since the front page narrowed to 'one head with an independently established role' -- had never been checked against the model's weights. D100 showed E123 established it by ATTENTION; nobody asked whether the OV circuit supports it
defects.operation: A THIRD INSTRUMENT, INDEPENDENT OF BOTH ATTENTION AND ABLATION, AND IT COSTS NOTHING. M[t,s] = W_E[t] . W_O_h . W_V_kv . W_E[s] plus a per-t bias term, over the 4 room tokens, for all 168 band heads; GQA means query head h uses KV head h//6, and tie_word_embeddings makes W_U = W_E. POSITIVE CONTROL PASSES: 16 of 168 heads map all four rooms to themselves, normalized diagonal dominance up to +2.4515, so the instrument can find copiers. THE TARGET FAILS: L22H7 scores diag_wins 1/4, which is chance, at -0.4949, RANK 140 OF 168, 17.3rd percentile. P6 AND THE DIRECTION IS STATED: this is the DIRECT path only -- no layernorm, no MLPs, no composition -- so a HIGH score is evidence of direct copying while a LOW score is NOT evidence of no copying. UNVERIFIED for 'not a copy head', not OVERTURNED. What it does establish is that the label was never weight-supported and nobody had looked. AND THREE INSTRUMENTS CONVERGE ON A DIFFERENT HEAD: L17H0 is in the published eight by attention, 4th of 168 under I_all ablation in R18, and 3rd of 168 here at +2.4383 with 4/4. That conjunction is POST HOC -- the top-6 was read after computing -- so it is registered as a falsifiable prediction against R19's crossed task, which does not yet exist and was built independently of the eight: L17H0 will rank in the top 10 of 168 by |centred tau^all| under signed_margin_drop

defects.defect: R19's full 64-base run died with torch.OutOfMemoryError at lm_head, 'Tried to allocate 4.38 GiB'. transformers materialises logits for EVERY position unless logits_to_keep is passed: batch 64 x ~250 tokens x 151936 vocab x 4 bytes is 9.7 GB, while the runner only ever reads logits[:, -1]. AND I CAUSED IT: raising --batch from 32 to 64 was described in a commit as 'a pure engineering parameter that changes no number'. It changed whether the job could run
defects.operation: AN ENGINEERING PARAMETER THAT MOVES THE FEASIBLE SET IS NOT FREE, and that is the lesson rather than the flag. Fixed with logits_to_keep=1 at all three forward sites, which changes no number because only the final position was ever read, and resubmitted at --batch 32 as well. THE SMOKE TEST COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT: n_base=2 is a single batch of 32, about 2.4 GB, so a smoke test that shrinks the batch does not exercise the memory path at all -- it verified the logic and silently certified nothing about scale. AND THE DIAGNOSIS EXISTS ONLY BECAUSE OF D95: the run was unbuffered, so the traceback survived; 232's buffered predecessor died leaving nothing but a weight-loading progress bar and its cause is still UNVERIFIED

defects.defect: D108 computed the OV copying circuit on the 4 ROOM tokens only, so its negative on L22H7 left an obvious alternative open: the head might copy OBJECTS or PERSONS instead, which would make the copy-head label wrong in a specific way rather than merely unsupported. And it left my own new hypothesis about L17H0 untested for specificity
defects.operation: RUN ON ALL THREE TOKEN SETS, and the confound written first was that scores are NOT comparable across sets because the sets have different embedding norms -- so every head is ranked WITHIN its own set. POSITIVE CONTROL PASSES ON ALL THREE: 16, 6 and 3 heads achieve perfect diagonal wins on rooms, objects and persons, with maximum normalized dominance +2.451, +3.446 and +3.128. The instrument is blind on none of them. L22H7 RANKS 140, 136 AND 149 OF 168 -- bottom quartile on all three. IT IS NOT A MISLABELLED COPIER; its direct OV path copies nothing in this task's vocabulary. AND THE SAME RUN WEAKENS MY OWN HYPOTHESIS FROM ONE STEP EARLIER: L17H0 is rank 3, 12 and 27, high on ALL THREE SETS, so it is a GENERIC direct copier rather than a room-specific mechanism. The registered prediction stands unchanged because it was about RANK under ablation, not about mechanism, but the mechanistic reading it invited is withdrawn. FINALLY L16H3, the largest ablation effect of the eight, ranks 146, 154 and 158 -- the loudest head under ablation is among the WORST direct copiers. THREE INSTRUMENTS NOW GIVE THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS, which is the two-instrument disagreement of D101 stated with one more instrument and no arbiter still

defects.defect: the repository had measured ONE of the three pairwise relationships between its instrument classes -- attention x ablation, R16's -0.1885 and -0.3952 -- and never the other two. So 'no arbiter' rested on a single edge of a triangle
defects.operation: THE TRIANGLE IS CLOSED AND EVERY EDGE IS NULL-TO-NEGATIVE. OV x ablation runs -0.14 to +0.22 pooled and about zero within layer, with the small pooled positive partly a layer artifact -- the within-layer means are -0.03 to -0.14 while ablation magnitude itself tracks layer at -0.24 and -0.33. attention x OV runs -0.0726 to -0.2430 pooled, and room_att x OV(rooms) survives the within-layer control at -0.1788: ATTENTION TO THE ROOM TOKEN ANTI-CORRELATES WITH THE OV CIRCUIT'S ABILITY TO COPY THE ROOM TOKEN. So the three ways this literature identifies a copy head -- it attends to the thing, ablating it hurts, its OV maps the thing to itself -- are mutually uninformative or mildly opposed on this task. THE CORRECT SCOPE, WHICH IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS: three instruments disagreeing does NOT mean all three are wrong. A head can attend to X, not copy X directly, and still matter causally through composition, so disagreement is EXPECTED if the mechanism is compositional. What follows is only that on this task these three operationalizations do not identify the same heads, and therefore none of them ALONE licenses the phrase 'the copy head'. Each is also a specific operationalization -- E132's final-position attention, zero-ablation at final or all positions, direct-path OV -- not attention or ablation in general. Both gauge checks ran: signed AND magnitude correlations for the OV edge, per D82, and a within-layer control for every edge

AND make verify COULD NEVER HAVE CAUGHT IT, because the gate runs on the system interpreter, 3.14, which is the one thing that can parse them. The check and the checked shared the only assumption that mattered
defects.operation: FOUND BY ACCIDENT, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING: headline.py was imported from a 3.11 virtualenv for an unrelated computation and refused to parse. Both sites rewritten without nested quotes -- one to a concatenation, one to percent formatting -- and the file now parses AND RUNS END TO END under 3.11.15 and 3.14.4, exit 0 on both. Every .py in the repository was then checked for the same pattern: 0 further failures. The front page's promise now names the two verified versions instead of saying 'a stock python3', because a claim about portability that was never tested on a second interpreter is not a portability claim

defects.defect: D108, D110 and D111 computed the OV circuit as W_E[t].W_O.W_V.W_E[s], omitting the final RMSNorm's learnable per-dimension scale model.norm.weight, which multiplies the unembedding side and IS the basis the logits are read in. That scale spans 2063x, from 0.0043 to 8.875 -- some dimensions are almost entirely suppressed before unembedding -- so it can reorder
defects.operation: THE RANKING IS ROBUST AND THE COUNTS ARE NOT. Spearman between bases is +0.9839, +0.9952 and +0.9926 on rooms, objects and persons, so the three prior steps are NOT in a materially wrong basis and their conclusions stand. BUT PERFECT-WINS NEARLY DOUBLES -- 16 to 25 on rooms, 6 to 11 on objects, 3 to 7 on persons -- so every ABSOLUTE count reported from that instrument was basis-dependent, AND L17H0 MOVES FROM RANK 3 TO RANK 11. That 3 was what made the three-instrument convergence striking, and the framing rested on it; the registered R19 prediction is unchanged because it is about ABLATION rank, but the annotation now sits beside it. GAUGE ARGUMENT, MADE BEFORE COMPUTING: the 1/||x|| half of RMSNorm is a per-DESTINATION scalar shared across every source, so it cannot reorder anything within a column -- only the learnable g can, which is why only g was applied. The frozen file now stores BOTH bases with scaled as primary. AND THE INFORMATIVE PART: g suppresses some dimensions by a factor of 2000 and the ranking still barely moves, so the OV copying signal is not concentrated in the suppressed directions

defects.defect: every instrument comparison in this repository -- D108, D110, D111, D113 -- was computed on qwen2.5-1.5b alone, so 'the three instruments are mutually uninformative' was an n=1 claim about a model. The OV circuit costs nothing to compute on a second model and R10/R18 already held that model's ablations; nobody had done it
defects.operation: REPLICATED ON qwen2.5-3b, 36 layers, 16 heads per layer, 288 band heads, scaled basis. ALL SIX OV x ablation EDGES SIT WITHIN +-0.07 -- pooled +0.0140 to +0.0658, within-layer -0.0359 to +0.0649 -- against -0.14 to +0.22 on 1.5b, so THE SECOND MODEL IS CLOSER TO ZERO, NOT FURTHER. The null is not a 1.5b idiosyncrasy. AND THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS STRONGER THERE: 45 heads copy all four rooms against 25 on 1.5b, 23 copy all eight objects, 15 copy all eight persons -- the instrument finds plenty of copiers, they are simply not the heads ablation flags. SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN 'TWO MODELS' SOUNDS AND THE PAGE SAYS SO: both are Qwen2.5, same family, same training data, same architecture, NOT independent draws. And the ATTENTION edges cannot be replicated at all because E132's scores exist only for 1.5b, so what replicates is the OV x ablation null while the attention edges remain n=1. Incidentally 3b's final RMSNorm scale spans 232x against 1.5b's 2063x, so the D113 basis correction matters less there

defects.defect: D108, D110, D111 and D114 all rested on the same positive control -- 'N heads map every token to itself, so the instrument can find copiers' -- and N was never tested against a null. If N is what matrix structure gives for free, THE POSITIVE CONTROL ITSELF IS VOID, and four negative results become silence from an instrument that had never returned a real non-zero. That is the exact failure this repository has a written rule against, committed four times against my own work
defects.operation: THE NULL IS A PER-HEAD COLUMN PERMUTATION, not (1/n)^n. Each column keeps its own argmax, so every head keeps its matrix structure and only the DIAGONAL ALIGNMENT is destroyed -- (1/n)^n would have assumed the argmaxes are independent, which they are not. 2000 permutations, both models, three token sets. qwen2.5-1.5b, 168 heads: rooms observed 25 against a null mean of 1.04 and a null MAX of 6; objects 11 against mean 0.00, max 1; persons 7 against mean 0.00, max 1. qwen2.5-3b, 288 heads: rooms 45 against mean 1.97, max 7; objects 23 against 0.00, max 1; persons 15 against 0.00, max 0. EVERY p IS AT THE FLOOR -- the observed count was never reached once in 2000 draws, on either model, on any set. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS REAL and the four negatives stand. AND THE FLOOR IS STATED RATHER THAN QUOTED AS PRECISION: p = 0.00050 is 1/2001 and means 'never in 2000', not a value resolved to five places

defects.defect: every number in this repository is conditioned on the band L14-27 with a sham of L0-7, and those are NOT complementary -- L8-13, seventy-two heads, is in neither and is silently excluded from every contrast. L14 was never chosen either; it is mechanically 'the upper half of 28'. The per-layer sd is 0.0891, 0.0913, 0.0882, 0.2231 at L12, L13, L14, L15, so the discontinuity is at L14->L15 and L14 belongs statistically with the low-variance side. Ranking all 25 possible boundaries by the ratio of mean sd above to below, L14 comes 11th, and the best cut is L8 -- exactly where the SHAM band ends. The sham boundary is well placed; the band boundary is not
defects.operation: MEASURED ACROSS FOUR WINDOWS AND THE RESULT IS MIXED, WHICH IS WHY BOTH HALVES ARE STATED. THE HEADLINE COUNT IS INVARIANT: 1 of 8 clears in L14-27, L15-27, L8-27 and all 28 layers alike. That is a real robustness to a choice that was never justified. WHAT IS NOT INVARIANT: the floor runs 0.3565 to 0.5032, which is 1.41x FROM THE WINDOW ALONE at fixed model, task, intervention and k -- a FIFTH transport axis, and the widest available without changing anything about the experiment. And the eight's ranks move materially even as percentiles: the last of them goes from the 96.4th percentile in the published band to the 87.8th over all 28 layers. FINALLY THE DISCARDED MIDDLE IS THE TRANSITION: L8-13's floor is 0.1560, twice the sham's 0.0792 and a third of the band's 0.4870, so excluding it was not neutral -- it removed the only region that could have shown where one regime becomes the other

defects.defect: 'three instruments, none privileged, no arbiter' -- D101, D110, D111 -- treated the three as three measurements of one quantity that happen to disagree. They are not. ATTENTION AND ABLATION ARE CONDITIONAL ON A PROMPT DISTRIBUTION; THE OV CIRCUIT IS NOT -- it is a statement about the weights and holds whatever the prompt. So they cannot disagree the way three thermometers disagree: they measure different objects, and the conclusion was right for the wrong reason
defects.operation: THE ASYMMETRY IS STATED AND IT IS NOT A PRIVILEGE. An instrument that ignores the task cannot say what a head does ON the task, so OV's task-invariance answers a different question rather than a better one. BUT THE ASYMMETRY MAKES SOMETHING FALSIFIABLE, and it is registered before the data: if a head's OV really maps room tokens to room tokens, ablating it should move the ROOM DISTRIBUTION even where it does not move the margin. R10 and R18 stored only the margin so this was untestable; R19 records room_set_kl as its second metric. The 25 OV-perfect room copiers are FROZEN into results/ov_perfect_room_copiers.json, and analyze.py -- written before the data and now extended before the data -- tests them against a matched-layer null of 25 over 50,000 draws. BOTH HALVES MUST HOLD: room_set_kl larger at one-sided p < 0.05 AND signed_margin_drop indistinguishable at p >= 0.05. A KL effect WITH a margin effect would mean the two metrics are redundant, not that OV has behavioural content; if neither holds, OV is a weight property with no behavioural correlate on this task and the 'third instrument' describes the matrix rather than the model's computation

defects.defect: the band-window row added one step earlier compared L14-27's floor against all 28 layers' and called the difference a WINDOW effect, but the two arms differ in the window AND in the sample size -- 168 heads against 336 -- and a 2-sigma estimate's own sampling error depends on n. That is exactly what this repository's own arm_contrast detector exists to catch, and I wrote the row without running it
defects.operation: THE CONTROL HOLDS n FIXED AND DESTROYS ONLY THE WINDOW STRUCTURE: resample 168 heads at random from all 336, 20,000 draws. Null median 0.3566, 2.5th 0.2648, 97.5th 0.4294, MAXIMUM 0.4639. Observed 0.4870 was NEVER REACHED, so the window effect is real and not a sample-size artifact -- the conclusion survives, but it was unsupported as written. AND THE MIRROR IS SHARPER THAN THE ORIGINAL CONTRAST: the sham window's floor is 0.0792 on 96 heads while a random 96 of 336 gives a median of 0.3552, which is 4.5x below. So EACH window is individually extreme against a size-matched random control, in opposite directions, which is a better statement of the layer effect than 'band vs sham 6.15x' -- a ratio between two extremes says nothing about which of them moved. p = 0.00005 is 1/20001 and means 'never in 20,000', not a value resolved to five places, the same floor caveat as D115

defects.defect: D108 introduced the OV circuit as 'a third instrument, independent of both attention and ablation' and D111 framed the result as 'attention captures where a head reads, not what it writes'. BOTH ARE THE ABSTRACT OF arXiv 2607.01002, Logit-Contribution Scoring Identifies Non-Literal Retrieval Heads, published 2026-07-01 -- AND THAT PAPER'S ID IS ALREADY CITED IN PAPER.md's OWN PRIOR-ART TABLE, filed under 'random-heads controls'. The repository read it as 'a paper that uses a random-heads control' and never as 'a paper whose contribution is the distinction I would later claim'. That is a label read as a description, committed against a citation already on the page, and NO PRIOR-ART CHECK WAS EVER RUN ON THE TRANSPORT OR OV CLAIMS despite P4 requiring one
defects.operation: LOCOS IS THE INSTRUMENT, BETTER FORMULATED. It scores each head by the projection of its OV-circuit output onto the ANSWER-TOKEN unembedding with a needle / off-needle contrast, which is sharper than the diagonal-dominance statistic used here, and it validates causally by mean-ablation across three model families rather than by correlation. WHAT IS VOID is the framing of D108, D110 and D111 as introducing something. WHAT IS NOT VOID is the measurements: L22H7 really does rank 140/136/149 of 168, and the permutation null really does put those counts beyond 20,000 draws. Independent re-derivation is not a contribution and the numbers are unaffected by learning that. WHAT MAY STILL BE THIS REPOSITORY'S is the transport result -- a random-component floor failing to carry across configurations while carrying perfectly across item samples -- which neither paper does. BUT AN ABSTRACT-LEVEL SEARCH CANNOT SETTLE THAT, which was written as the confound BEFORE this search ran and is the same reason the original novelty premise died. UNVERIFIED, not novel. The search's positive control fired: it returned two squarely relevant papers alongside malware detection and crowd counting, so it was noisy but not silent

defects.defect: D119 left the transport result as the one possibly-novel claim here, marked UNVERIFIED because the query that killed the OV claim was not aimed at it. Aimed properly it lands three times: 2407.08734 'Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics are not Robust' (2024-07) says existing methods are highly sensitive to seemingly insignificant changes in the ablation methodology and that the task a circuit is required to perform depends on the ablation used to test it; 2309.16042 'Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching' (2023-09) says varying metrics and corruption methods could lead to disparate interpretability results; and 2510.00845 'Mechanistic Interpretability as Statistical Estimation' (2025-10) says the causal effect of a component is a VOLATILE RANDOM VARIABLE RATHER THAN A FIXED PROPERTY and that small perturbations in input data or hyperparameters yield vastly different circuits. THE LAST IS THIS REPOSITORY'S THESIS, IN AN ABSTRACT, NINE MONTHS BEFORE IT STARTED
defects.operation: THE PROJECT HAS NO ESTABLISHED NOVELTY CLAIM. The floor result, the instrument comparison and the transport framing each have published prior art, and in two of three cases the paper was already cited here or trivially findable. WHAT IT STILL IS: a worked audit of one prior experiment, carried out in public, with an unusually complete error record -- and that is a CASE STUDY, not a contribution to method. AND THE SEARCH DISCIPLINE IS PART OF THE FINDING: the first transport query returned ten papers on dialogue contradiction, document expansion and pronoun resolution, zero relevant, which was SILENCE FROM A BADLY PHRASED QUERY rather than evidence of absence -- the same tool had returned two squarely relevant papers minutes earlier. An abstract search that finds nothing is not a null; it is an unfit instrument until a working query proves otherwise, and I have now been wrong in that direction twice

defects.defect: R19's full run had been in a RESTART LOOP and I did not see it. Tasks 242, 249, 251 and 253 all carry the same label: each start ran until the box SIGKILLed it -- 242 lasted 71 minutes and died at layer 13 of 28 -- and each restart began again at LAYER 1, so no run ever finished. I reported 'layer 13/28' in three consecutive steps while the process behind it had been dead for 25 minutes: the log tail of a killed job is IDENTICAL to the log tail of a slow one, and I read the log instead of the process. D95's lesson was 'read by label, not by id'; the lesson I actually needed was 'READ THE PROCESS, NOT THE LOG', and the id-grep habit hid three of the four restarts
defects.operation: THE CAUSE OF THE KILLS IS STILL UNVERIFIED -- 232 at 22m47s and 242 at 71m, both 'killed by system or user', no traceback even under -u, with 42 GB host RAM free and GPU headroom. What is fixable is the COST, and it was total: a kill threw away the entire run. ADDED PER-LAYER ATOMIC CHECKPOINTING -- the partial cells, the completed-layer set and the saturation flip counters are written to <out>.ckpt after every layer via a temp file and an atomic replace, so a kill mid-write cannot leave a truncated checkpoint, and a checkpoint whose code_version or n_prompts disagree is REFUSED rather than mixed into a new run. POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE RECOVERY PATH, because an untested recovery mechanism is exactly the instrument that has never returned non-zero: SIGKILLed a 28-layer run at layer 12, confirmed the checkpoint held 12 layers, 288 cells and the flip counters, reran and saw 'RESUMING from checkpoint: 12 layers already done', ran to layer 28, got saturation 0.4% IDENTICAL to the uninterrupted run, 672 of 672 cells, and the checkpoint deleted itself on success

defects.defect: centred_null()'s interpretive clause inverted the sign of this repository's central quantity, and PAPER.md's copy of the same paragraph already carried a correction (D90) that walked past it
defects.operation: R10_exhaustive/run.py:281 is drops[name].append(bm - margin(enc, cor)), so a POSITIVE drop means the ablated margin is LOWER -- the ablation HURT. The page read '+0.0479 ... ablating a random late-layer head IMPROVES the correct-answer margin more often than it hurts, 100 of 168'. Every number is right; one word inverts all of them, turning an unremarkable fact into a striking one. The centring statistic is SIGN-INDEPENDENT so no count moved, which is why proofreading the numbers could never have caught it. Corrected reading: L16H3 (-0.4668) and the copy head L22H7 (-0.1317) are heads the model does BETTER without on this task. The check also produced an unclaimed cross-experiment positive control: R10 reproduces all 8 of E132b's published effects, 8 of 8 in sign, max ratio deviation from 1 of 0.0001.

defects.defect: README.md stated the defect ledger held 120 rows while it held 122, and the sentence carrying the error is the one advertising the completeness of the error record
defects.operation: Found by an INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL READER, not by any instrument here -- the first defect in this repository located by something other than its author or his own detectors. Both checkers are structurally blind to it: headline.py --check compares the EMITTER against a hardcoded constant and never reads this sentence, while detectors/prose_numbers.py compares PROSE against the emitter but cannot see bare integers -- a blind spot it declares and asserts in its own selftest case 7.
