defects.defect: set_enrichment()'s positive control is an arithmetic identity, so the repository's central null had no valid positive control
defects.operation: An independent adversarial reviewer found it. top8 is by construction the argmax of the test statistic over all 8-head subsets of the band, and every null draw is an 8-head subset of the same band, so T(null) <= T(top8) with probability 1. It measures nothing about power. Replaced with a planted-enrichment power curve: calibration at delta=0 fires at 0.0433 against a nominal 0.05, MDE80 = 0.9136 sd = 0.2225 margin units, observed enrichment of the eight -0.1226 sd. The claim moves from UNVERIFIED to a BOUNDED ABSENCE. The pre-registered decision rule was itself defective -- 'observed >= MDE80 -> informative' can never return informative for a true null, a check that could only fail, written inside a pre-registration.

defects.defect: the front page's '22-24% recovery' quotes a ratio of signal-to-noise ratios, not effect recovery; its median cell is sign-inverted; and the intersection of informative, valid and sign-consistent cells is empty
defects.operation: Found by an independent adversarial reviewer, all three verified against R6's own JSONs. (1) rr = (|pc|/band_sd)_arm / (|pc|/band_sd)_zero carries the factor band_sd_zero/band_sd_arm; the prose describes |pc_arm|/|pc_zero|. Median over informative cells: rr 0.2368 vs recovery 0.1199. (2) qwen2.5-3b's zero control is +1.60537 while mean and resample are NEGATIVE; R7 and R8 exclude sign-inverted arms and R6 never did, because pc_clears_own_floor tests magnitude only. That cell sets the published median. (3) informative AND round_valid AND sign_consistent = 0 of 4 cells; the page disclosed the first two counts and never the empty intersection. Corrected reading makes the off-manifold limitation WORSE: median recovery over informative and sign-consistent cells is 0.1359, so ~85% of the zeroing effect is not the head's contribution, not 76%.

defects.defect: the per-layer checkpoint has NO CONCURRENCY GUARD, and I queued a second runner against the same --out path while the first was still running
defects.operation: run.py resumes by reading <out>.ckpt and writes it back after every layer via a temp file plus Path.replace. That is atomic against a KILL but not against a SECOND RUNNER: two processes resuming the same checkpoint would each hold their own done_layers set in memory and each write the whole file, so whichever finishes a layer last silently erases the other's progress and the surviving cells dict is a mixture of two runs. Caught because pueue showed task 262 RUNNING under label R19-RESUME-from-22 while my task 269 sat QUEUED to run the identical command on the identical path -- I had submitted duplicates because I was tracking my own submissions from memory instead of listing the queue by label, which is the third variant of the same defect after D95 and D121. 269 removed before it could start. The guard is NOT added in the same step because editing run.py while 262 is running would make its result file's source stamp STALE -- the hazard validate_provenance.py exists to surface.

defects.defect: nine R19 deaths were attributed to the machine SIGKILLing long GPU jobs, on the sole evidence that pueue reported Killed with no Python traceback -- and a second agent session preempting the GPU queue is a better-supported explanation that was never considered
defects.operation: THE PROXY WAS USED BACKWARDS. 'no traceback => an external SIGKILL' is sound; 'external SIGKILL => the box or the OOM killer' is NOT, and only the second was ever used. What is CONFIRMED: a live process from a different Claude session, working in the coval-deep-analysis project, carried the literal command string 'pueue kill 260; sleep 8; gpu-run ... r46 ...', observed in the process table; and the pueue id sequence alternates strictly -- 254 R19 then 255/256/257 CoVal, 258 R19 then 259, 260 R19 then 261, 262 R19 then 263-268 -- so five of five R19 terminations are immediately succeeded by that session's jobs. What stays UNVERIFIED: that this caused EVERY death, since 232 and 242 predate any observed CoVal activity and dmesg is unreadable without privilege, so OOM cannot be excluded. What is OVERTURNED: 'the box SIGKILLs long GPU jobs' as the sole explanation -- it was never established, only inferred from silence. Ivan's standing rule that his tasks preempt the queue was written for HIS tasks; two agent sessions both applying it is a livelock, and the correct response is to queue behind rather than retaliate.

defects.defect: task 270 read as 'Queued, waiting its turn' for 17 minutes while the pueue GPU GROUP was PAUSED and the GPU sat idle -- it would have waited forever
defects.operation: `pueue status` showed 270 Queued and nothing Running; nvidia-smi showed no compute apps. The enclosing state was 'Group "gpu" (1 parallel): paused', set by another session. A task's status is meaningless without its group's. THIS IS THE FOURTH VARIANT OF ONE DEFECT: D95 read a status WORD for a job that had ended two hours earlier; D121 read a LOG TAIL for a process dead 25 minutes; D126 read MY OWN MEMORY of submissions instead of the queue; D128 read a task's status without the group's. The unifying statement is that each read a LOCAL indicator without its ENCLOSING state -- a task inside a group, a log inside a process, a submission inside a queue. Resolved with `pueue start -g gpu`; 270 began immediately.

defects.defect: the checkpoint's own version guard makes the runner UNIMPROVABLE while a long job is partially done -- the fix that would let the job survive costs the work the guard protects
defects.operation: _CODE_VERSION is sha256(run.py)[:8] and the resume path refuses any checkpoint whose version differs, on the correct reasoning that mixing two code versions' cells is a silent corruption. After ten preemptions the job stands at 26 of 28 layers with 26 and 27 -- both INSIDE the band the four hypotheses are scoped to -- still missing. The obvious repair is a --layers range so each attempt finishes one layer inside the ~5-20 minute window between preemptions, plus an O_EXCL lock for D126. BOTH REQUIRE EDITING run.py, WHICH DISCARDS ALL 26 LAYERS. The guard is not wrong; the tension is real and general: a version-hashed checkpoint creates lock-in exactly when a job is long enough to need one. Resolved by resubmitting UNMODIFIED and deferring both improvements until the run lands, because bypassing the guard on the grounds that 'this edit changes no number' is the same claim I made about batch 32 to 64, which changed whether the job could run at all.

defects.defect: `pueue kill -g` and `pueue kill -a` PAUSE the group as a documented side effect, so every submission after a group-kill sits Queued forever -- and D127 attributed the resulting stalls to an adversarial second session
defects.operation: Read from `pueue kill --help` on pueue 4.0.4: '-g, --group <GROUP>  Kill all running tasks in a group. This also pauses the group' and '-a, --all ... This also pauses all groups'. I resumed the gpu group at D128, and 25 minutes later it was paused again with my task 273 Queued and the card idle -- so D128's 'another session left it paused' was a one-off framing of a RECURRING mechanism. The kills recorded in D127 are real and directly observed, but the STALLS are a documented flag behaviour, not additional hostility, and the other session's own job 268 shows Failed(1) for the same reason. CORRECTS D127's attribution and corrects a standing rule in memory: 'kill and restart, never pause' is unachievable with the group form, because THE KILL IS A PAUSE. Checked my own wrapper first -- /home/ivan/.local/bin/gpu-run never calls pause, so it was not mine.

defects.defect: R19's saturation gate counts cells where the correct room is not the argmax, which is already true for every baseline-INCORRECT item -- so its floor is the baseline error rate and it measures almost nothing about the ablation
defects.operation: run.py:347 is `nflip += int((am < 0).sum())` with am = correct_logit - best_other_logit. R19 does NOT filter to baseline-correct items (R10 does, at run.py:274), and its baseline accuracy is 0.7412, i.e. an error rate of 0.2588. Observed flip rates: final 0.2587, all 0.2616 -- the final-scope value sits 0.0001 BELOW the baseline error rate and the all-scope value 0.0028 above it. The gate's pre-registered refusal at >50% therefore tests a quantity whose floor is set by the task's difficulty, not by the intervention, and on any task with >50% baseline error it would refuse regardless of what the ablation does. WHAT SURVIVES: metric index 2, `fl = (argmax != baseline_argmax)`, IS correctly referenced to the baseline argmax and is unaffected -- the data to do this right is present and the analysis uses it. WHAT THE CORRECTED READING SUGGESTS, stated as an observation and not a result because the counter is a NET (an ablation can also FIX a baseline-wrong item, reducing the count): once the floor is subtracted, I_final changes the answer on essentially no additional cells and I_all on about 0.28 percentage points. Found before the analysis ran; not fixed in run.py because D129 -- editing it would discard 27 of 28 layers.

defects.defect: the L17H0 head-level bet was registered in prose and never given a scorer -- analyze.py, written before the data specifically so the analysis could not be tuned to it, did not compute the one prediction the pre-registration staked a head on
defects.operation: PREREGISTRATION.md stakes L17H0 on the top 10 of 168 by |centred tau^all| under signed_margin_drop and says 'if it fails, the three-instrument convergence was a coincidence over 168 heads and this line is the record that I bet on it'. When the data landed I had to compute the rank by hand from a scratchpad script, which is the mode this repository files against everyone else. A REGISTERED BET NOBODY SCORES IS NOT REGISTERED -- writing the analysis before the data protects against tuning, and it protects against nothing if a registered quantity is missing from it. Scorer added to analyze.py; the bet is WRONG, rank 37 of 168 under I_all and 45 under I_final.

defects.defect: the disattenuation ceiling was the PEARSON reliability of the SIGNED effect applied to a SPEARMAN over CENTRED MAGNITUDES -- wrong coefficient family and wrong quantity, biased toward flattering the conclusion
defects.operation: analyze.py:187 correlates |tau - mu| with Spearman; split_half() measured Pearson reliability of signed tau, and signed_margin_drop's value was additionally applied to the other two metrics. Taking |centred| destroys information so the signed reliability is HIGHER, every disattenuated value came out LOWER, and the gap to 0.9 looked safer than it is. Correct ceilings 0.9434/0.9863/0.9056 against 0.9904/0.9990/0.9849; primary metric's correction understated by 0.0341. Conclusion unchanged, all three still below 0.9. The Spearman/Pearson half was predicted as ADVERSARY A19; THE WRONG-QUANTITY HALF WAS NOT PREDICTED and surfaced only while chasing A19. An independent reviewer re-derived the replacement to 4 decimals.

defects.defect: R19's README said H-support 'fails all four components on all three metrics', contradicted by the table six lines above it
defects.operation: published_agree requires 8/8 and observes 7/8, 8/8, 8/8 -- it PASSES on room_set_kl and behavioural_flip. Ten of twelve components fail, not twelve. No instrument here can catch it: the claim is a count in prose over a table the emitter never sums.

defects.defect: the one H-support component that passes is an agreement between two nulls
defects.operation: agree counts heads where (|centred| > floor) matches across scopes. None of the eight clears either floor on room_set_kl or behavioural_flip, so every agreement scored is False == False. The check registers 8/8 whenever the intervention is too weak to move any of the eight past the floor on either arm, and cannot distinguish 'the two supports agree' from 'neither detects anything'.

defects.defect: the component that actually decides H-position was on no page, and the box explaining H-position had been deleted by one of my own slice edits without my noticing
defects.operation: H-position has three registered components. The third, Spearman(line-0 rank, position-averaged rank) >= 0.8, reads 0.3494 -- missing by 0.4506, seventeen times the ICC margin the page framed the verdict on -- and is -0.2541 and -0.1903 on the other metrics. defects.defect: the README claimed the 23 MB result file 'is checked in' and git ls-files did not list it; two further files headline.py consumes had no emitter anywhere in the repository
defects.operation: An independent reviewer ran git ls-files; no instrument here did. r19_crossed_qwen2.5-1.5b.json was untracked while the Reproduce section pointed at it. And r19_split_half_reliability.json and r19_reliability_of_magnitude.json -- THE TWO NUMBERS THAT CLOSE THIS ROUND'S HEADLINE ESCAPE HATCH -- were produced by a scratchpad script and generated by nothing checked in. headline.py's own opening paragraph says a claim whose generator does not exist is indistinguishable from a claim that was never true; it was true of its own two most load-bearing files. Result file tracked; emitters added under R19_crossed_position_support/tools/.

defects.defect: the 64 base instances are not exchangeable, so the cluster bootstrap CIs are roughly 2.3x too narrow and the effective n is about 12
defects.operation: query = elig[b%8] and want = rooms[b%4] with 4|8, so the query name perfectly determines the answer room: 8 distinct (query, answer) cells replicated 8x. A reviewer measured the between-group share of base-level tau variance at median 0.669 against a random-grouping null of 0.094, giving ICC ~0.62, design effect 1+7rho = 5.35 and effective n ~12. The percentile bootstrap is also mis-centred, the point estimate sitting at the 83.8th percentile of its own draws. Predicted as A14 and again as A17; CONFIRMED and now quantified. Does NOT overturn H-support -- a CI 2.3x wider still lands nowhere near 0.9.

defects.defect: the split-half reliability is reported for the ONE split that is balanced on both design factors, and other splits of the same data give 0.0240 and -0.3697
defects.operation: bases 0-31 vs 32-63 holds all 8 query names 4x and all 4 rooms 8x in each half, so it measures replicate noise only. Splitting by ROOM gives +0.0240 (final) and +0.4697 (all); even/odd gives -0.3697 and +0.2025. Only the maximum over splits is published, so the ceiling is over-stated and the disattenuation under-corrects. The file's own random_split_lo_final = 0.5458 already implies a ceiling near 0.80 and a disattenuated 0.848 -- inside arguing distance of the registered 0.9.

defects.defect: icc1() is ICC(1,1), the one-way model, on a fully crossed base-by-position design where ICC(3,1) is the appropriate estimator
defects.operation: Every base is measured at the SAME 8 positions, so the design is crossed and ICC(1,1) charges the position MAIN EFFECT to error -- and there is a large one, baseline_margin_by_pos spanning 4.02 to 0.51. Recomputed by a reviewer from the same base_pos cells: 0.4737 -> 0.5616 for signed_margin_drop, which CROSSES the registered 0.50 threshold. THE HALF-FIX IS FARTHER FROM THE TRUTH THAN THE ORIGINAL ERROR -- matching only the denominator, which is literally what the reviewer's finding asks for, puts the `all` scope below 1 and would have retracted a claim the matched comparison supports. defects.defect: 31 registered decision rules at alpha 0.05 with no multiplicity correction anywhere -- A18, confirmed by two reviewers and left standing
defects.operation: The obvious repair had to be refused. A correction lowers alpha, which makes a PRESENCE rule (fires when p <= alpha) harder and an ABSENCE rule EASIER -- and R19's H-position is registered literally as `p_pos >= ALPHA`, so failing to reject is a PASS condition, as is 'the eight are not enriched' at p = 0.8069. A blanket Bonferroni would have STRENGTHENED this repository's central claims with no new observation. detectors/multiplicity.py therefore splits the family by direction before correcting, derives the inventory by walking the emitter rather than hand-listing it (48 p-values: 14 PRESENCE, 21 ABSENCE, 10 RESOLUTION, 3 CONTROL, 0 UNCLASSIFIED), and reports the family-size-free m_break = floor(alpha/p) because the family size is bookkeeping (12? 31? 33?). Registered verdict MULTIPLICITY-BITES: 5 of 13 firing presence verdicts die below a family of 6 -- mechanism.alignment (m_break 1), set_enrichment L17H0 (1), selection_overlap sum-ratio (3), L22H7 one-head (4), mean-of-ratios (5). AND THE SHAPE IS WORSE THAN THE COUNT: all 8 survivors are pinned at their own null's resolution floor, so m_break measures how many draws were bought, not effect size; n_surviving_with_graded_p = 0. The feared outcome did not occur: 0 absence verdicts would be manufactured, smallest absence p = 0.0704, so no correction at any family size can create or destroy one. Not a retraction -- a scope: these hold if the tests you count are the ones in their own round.

defects.defect: detectors/prose_numbers.py was blind to scientific notation in BOTH directions, and had been for the whole life of the repository
defects.operation: Found by a true number reading as unbacked: the front page quoted 0.0000499975 against a generator that emits exactly that value. The tokenizer's regex had no exponent alternation, and json.dump writes small floats in scientific notation. Measured on the live reference set: 21 distinct emitted values were invisible, so prose quoting any of them raised a FALSE ALARM -- and in the unsound direction the regex shredded each into fragments, putting 26 mantissas and bare exponents ('05','06','09') into the BACKING set as if they had been emitted, so a prose number could be backed by an exponent. backs() carried the same bug a second time: it computed the prose's precision as digits-after-the-dot, which is 2 for '1.93e-08', then rounded the generated value to two decimals -- 0.0 -- and rejected a correct quotation. Both fixed, selftest re-run, power re-measured (36.76% unchanged on x.xx, 27.39 -> 27.41 on xx.x). THE TIGHTENED DETECTOR IMMEDIATELY FLAGGED 13 PROSE NUMBERS ACROSS THREE FILES THAT HAD NEVER BEEN CHECKED. Nine were backed by emitting the control magnitudes they quote; four are exempted with a written reason, because hook_identity loads a model and the reference set is deliberately dependency-free.
